intervention.factor: one extra KL(base||policy) anchor term in the action loss of arm B only
intervention.control: arm A = R16 unweighted arm: unchanged tactical_policy_loss, no added term, same seed schedule
intervention.anchor: arm B = bit-identical to arm A except L_total=L_original+1.0*KL_anchor over every action_valid row
unchanged: fresh seed reset before every construction
intervention.weight_tuning: none: 1.0 fixed before the run, never adjusted on any result

formula.text: Arm B only, weight fixed at 1.0 before the run. For a full-80 batch let a=policy_logits [1,80,18], b=the frozen baseline policy_logits of the same encoded rows (detached, no gradient into the backbone), V={i: action_valid_i and sequence-valid_i}, N=|V|, and KL_anchor=(1/N)*sum_{i in V} sum_c softmax(b_i)_c*(log softmax(b_i)_c-log softmax(a_i)_c), i.e. KL(base||policy) in nats averaged over every action_valid row (F.kl_div(log_target=True, reduction="batchmean") on the masked rows). L_total(B)=L_original+1.0*KL_anchor. L_total(A)=L_original, byte-identical to the R16 unweighted arm. L_original is the unchanged tactical_policy_loss (action 1.0, option .2, target .5, termination .2, slack .1, local 1.0) and its local term is exactly the same KL(base||policy) form; that term is empty here because the R10 action-only batches contain zero local_valid rows, so it contributes exactly 0 to both arms. This is an intentional single-factor loss/structure revision of the planned L_local_KL, which was specified for explicit local-regression samples: R17 keeps its functional form and applies it to the action_valid rows as an anchor to the frozen base policy. The weight is never tuned on any result.

extension_of.planned_term: L_local_KL on explicit local-regression samples (local_valid mask)
extension_of.implementation: the same KL(base||policy) functional form applied to the action_valid mask

data_fact.note: the frozen tactical_policy_loss local term is KL(base||policy) on this mask; the action-only R10 data leaves it empty, so it is exactly 0 in both arms

extension_of.classification: intentional single-factor structural/loss revision, frozen before the run

train.data: original R10 train 8 events only; validation 8 never trained and never used for weights/epochs/selection
train.order: original train order roundrobin step modulo8; 25 visits each

initialization.method: fresh seed reset immediately before every N1 construction after backbone load; both arms use the identical N1 config, so the same seed must give a byte-identical initial head state; no warmstart, no checkpoint, no round15/16 weights
initialization.reproducibility_check: arm A final head SHA is compared per seed with the R16 unweighted final head SHA and recorded; a mismatch would be reported, not silently retrained

features: one genuine CUDA batch16 encode pass over the original 16x80 rows, shared RAM tensors between all six arms, no disk feature cache
precision: FP32 no AMP, matmul TF32 false, cuDNN TF32 false, float32 precision highest in encode/train/evaluate/closed-loop

confirmation_worlds.construction: tactical_teacher_validation.ValidationWorld via make_world; same advance/firing/canonical geometry as R8/R9/R11/R16; split field is confirmation

constant_filter.rule: Per-world construction filter, executed before any training and frozen in this preregistration: a candidate world is rejected when hold (candidate 0), constant right (candidate 3, +2 px/frame) or constant left (candidate 7, -2 px/frame) alone completes it feasibly. Rejected groups are regenerated in index order from the pre-declared replacement pool (each replacement is probed first and skipped if it is itself constant-solvable or duplicates a previous-round parameter signature) and the whole 24-world set is re-probed until every world fails all three constants. Reason: R16 confirmation worlds were passed by constant right 9/24 in aggregate (F1 8/8 by right and by left, F2 4/8 by hold), so an unfiltered aggregate cannot be read as a capability measure. The probe runs the frozen advance() dynamics with a fixed action sequence: no pixels, no labels, no teacher, no solver, no program search, no witness.
constant_filter.executor: frozen advance() from tactical_teacher_validation, the same step function the closed-loop runner uses; fixed action sequences only

confirmation_worlds.usage: closed-loop confirmation only; never trained, never used for weight/epoch/model selection, no teacher label created

closed_loop.runner: unchanged R11 run_event / pixel_stack / render_state / executed_history; sticky collision, continue full horizon; per-event hidden reset
closed_loop.b0: same renderer and runner with the frozen baseline policy logits only; a reference on these renders, not a real B0 capability measurement
closed_loop.order: all six checkpoints trained and SHA-frozen first; only then B0 confirmation, then each arm-seed confirmation, then the old 8 validation continuity control
closed_loop.metrics: per event feasible/survived/goal/firsthit; per family event counts; decisions, raw-unsupported and invalid counts; per arm action distribution (hold/right/left share, median switches)
closed_loop.families: the 24-event aggregate is reported for reference only; conclusions are read per family and on the F2+F3 subset

forgetting.definition: forgetting = B0 F1 feasible count minus the arm F1 feasible count on the same 24 confirmation renders; positive means the finetune lost base F1 behaviour, negative means it gained F1 successes B0 does not have
forgetting.reference: B0 measured once on these renders with the frozen baseline logits only
forgetting.caveat: after the constant filter B0 is expected to fail most F1 worlds, so a non-positive forgetting value does not mean the arm kept a base behaviour

order_of_operations: CPU tests first; freeze this prereg second; one training run of six checkpoints third; evaluate only after all six exist; report last
failure_policy: retain first failure; one fixed run, no extra epochs, no baseline switch, no weight change, no overwrite
